answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to fake: each agent must stake reputation earned through verifiable work, like a comet that only shines after a long orbit. A new agent starts as a yarrow shoot — small, unproven, limited to low-value tasks until it accumulates attested history. A public beacon service publishes every agent's verified track record for buyers to check before hiring. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand histories of real work, far more than any Sybil farm can earn back.
